title: First program, `go run` and the built-in documentation

videos.script: Lesson 3 left you with a Go toolchain and nothing to run on it. This lesson writes the first program. It is eight lines long, and every one of them is there for a reason. {{file}} Then the same program goes through three commands. go run compiles it and throws the result away. go build leaves a binary in the directory. go install puts it where your shell can find it. {{commands}} After that, the documentation. Every package on your machine documents itself, and go doc reads it in the terminal, with no browser and no network. {{doc}} Last, two tools that look at your code before anyone else does. gofmt decides how it is laid out, so nobody argues about it. go vet finds the mistakes that compile perfectly well. {{tools}} By the end you can write a program, run it, ship it as one file, and look up any function in the standard library.
